themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 18 this week versus a baseline of 2.5 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 620% increase (z-score: 4.38)—suggesting a coordinated or sudden surge in graffiti, unlicensed advertising, or political signage across Borough Park/Kensington.
evidence: 18 illegal posting complaints this week vs. 2.5 weekly baseline (620% spike, z-score: 4.38)
Statistically significant deviation flagged as 'high severity'
No prior social media or community board chatter suggests sudden, concentrated event
reporting_angles: Ground canvass of major commercial corridors (18th Avenue, 86th Street) to document what type of illegal postings are driving complaints
Interview 311 complaint filers and local business owners to establish timeline and whether postings are political, commercial, or graffiti-related

themes_detail.label: Construction/Plumbing Complaint Explosion
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints jumped to 59 last week versus a 17.5 weekly average—a 237% increase (z-score: 7.31)—indicating either widespread unpermitted work, permit violations, or burst pipes/water damage affecting multiple buildings in the district.
evidence: 59 construction/plumbing complaints last week vs. 17.5 weekly baseline (237% spike, z-score: 7.31)
622 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days; 328 are alterations, suggesting active renovation activity
Community board has repeatedly requested 'additional building inspectors' in budget requests, indicating chronic inspection capacity shortage
reporting_angles: Query DOB database to identify which properties filed permits in the spike week and whether complaints are clustered in one neighborhood block
Interview DOB inspectors about staffing levels and whether they can keep pace with renovation filings; tie to community board's long-standing request for inspector expansion

themes_detail.label: Building Use Code Violations
themes_detail.summary: Building/use complaints exploded to 134 three weeks ago versus a 7.2 weekly baseline—a 1748% spike (z-score: 24.31, highest severity flagged)—suggesting either illegal conversions, overcrowding, zoning violations, or unlicensed businesses triggering a wave of enforcement complaints.
evidence: 134 building/use complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 7.2 weekly baseline (1748% spike, z-score: 24.31, highest severity)
Active ULURP application at 39th Street & New Utrecht Avenue signals neighborhood zoning tension
137 new building permits and 78 ALT-CO filings in 90 days indicate active development/conversion pipeline
reporting_angles: Investigate whether complaints cluster around specific blocks or property types; cross-reference with active real estate transactions to identify conversion activity
Interview DOB and residents to understand what violations are being reported—illegal subdivisions, unlicensed short-term rentals, overcrowded housing, or zoning misuse

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Spike
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 14 two weeks ago versus a 1.8 weekly baseline—a 700% increase (z-score: 6.61)—suggesting either increased unlicensed street vending, food cart violations, or a neighborhood crackdown creating resident pushback.
evidence: 14 vendor enforcement complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.8 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score: 6.61)
Spike is statistically significant but complaints have since moderated, suggesting concentrated event or campaign
High Orthodox Jewish and immigrant populations in Borough Park/Kensington may drive complaints about informal street commerce
reporting_angles: Determine whether spike reflects increased violations or increased reporting; interview community members about vendor activity on key commercial streets
Investigate whether city enforcement campaign triggered the spike or whether residents are protesting new vending activity

themes_detail.label: Traffic & Bike Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Traffic complaints rose to 6 two weeks ago (500% above 1.0 weekly baseline, z-score: 5.77) and bike/roller/skate complaints hit 3 (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)—together suggesting new traffic hazards, unsafe street conditions, or a recent incident triggering complaints.
evidence: Traffic complaints: 6 two weeks ago vs. 1.0 weekly baseline (500% spike, z-score: 5.77)
Bike/roller/skate complaints: 3 two weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
Both categories show extreme z-scores, indicating rare, concentrated event rather than gradual trend
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify whether spikes cluster around a specific intersection or street; correlate with any recent traffic signal outages (361 complaints on record) or construction
Interview residents and local cyclists about what changed two weeks ago—new hazards, reduced signal timing, or influx of delivery/scooter traffic
